body:
EQT stock gained 1.23 percent on September 21, 2026, while its Asia vehicle broadens private-market access. Assets under management reached EUR 270 billion in 2025.

EQT AB (SE0012853455) closed at SEK 304.00 on September 21, 2026, gaining 1.23 percent over five trading days as the private-markets manager expanded its Asia strategy. The move followed the launch of EQT Nexus Asia, an evergreen vehicle designed to offer access to the firm's private-capital platform across several Asia Pacific markets.

According to Simply Wall St on September 22, 2026, EQT launched EQT Nexus Asia for eligible individual and institutional investors. The vehicle covers healthcare, services, technology and industrial technology investments in India, Korea, Japan, Greater China, Southeast Asia and Australia and New Zealand.

The structure matters because evergreen funds can provide recurring management-fee income while widening access beyond traditional institutional mandates. The same September 22, 2026 analysis put expected annual revenue growth at 17.1 percent and expected annual earnings growth at 30.3 percent over the next three years, although those figures are analyst forecasts rather than reported results.

MarketScreener reported that EQT had EUR 270 billion in assets under management at the end of fiscal year 2025. Its 2025 sales table showed EUR 1.64 billion from private capital and EUR 1.05 billion from real assets, compared with EUR 1.36 billion and EUR 952 million respectively in 2024.

That comparison implies private-capital revenue increased by EUR 280 million, or 20.6 percent, from 2024 to 2025, while real-assets revenue rose by EUR 98 million, or 10.3 percent. The figures place the Asia launch within a larger fee-growth platform rather than treating it as a stand-alone event.

The September 22, 2026 analysis also identified fundraising and deployment pace as near-term earnings drivers. It described product expansion and the broader Asia and United States footprint as sources of execution, regulatory and geopolitical complexity.

For investors, the key tension is therefore quantitative: EQT's 2025 private-capital sales were 20.6 percent higher than in 2024, while the new vehicle still has to convert wider distribution into client uptake and recurring fees. That conversion is not yet represented by a reported Nexus Asia revenue figure.

EQT closed at SEK 304.00 on Nasdaq Stockholm on September 21, 2026. MarketScreener listed a 52-week closing reference of EUR 26.92 and an average analyst target of EUR 35.22, implying a displayed spread of 30.86 percent; those figures use a different currency presentation from the Stockholm reference price and are not combined into a price comparison.
